shipped_originals.title_o: Composite faces are not (necessarily) processed coactively: A test using systems factorial technology and logical-rule models.

blind_target.title: Information-processing alternatives to holistic perception: identifying the mechanisms of secondary-level holism within a categorization paradigm.
blind_target.evidence_quote:
To further investigate the difference in these findings, we extend our investigation
of face processing to schematic faces similar to Fifić and Townsend’s (2010) using the
paradigm developed in Cheng et al. (2018). Unlike the morphed faces in Cheng et al.
(2018) in which the category of the face depended on the observer’s perception of the
similarity between faces, the schematic faces are made up of fixed values that represent the
differences between the space between the eyes and the space between the nose and the
lips. We again employ SFT in order to determine whether there is any evidence for holistic
processing.
blind_target.outcome_quote:
Importantly, while the faces we used appear to be processed holistically in the stan-
dard composite task, there is no consistent evidence for coactivity when participants cate-
gorize upright aligned faces. We also did not find that upright faces are treated differently
from misaligned or inverted faces. Based on our non-parametric and parametric results, we
can also see that the main differences between the face conditions were quantitative rather
than qualitative (see Richler, Wong, & Gauthier, 2011)).
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The paper explicitly investigates the discrepancy between Fific and Townsend’s coactivity finding and Cheng et al. using schematic faces, with a stated prediction about reproducing the former. Experiment 2 finds no consistent coactivity, contrary to that target finding. This is a retest by relationship, despite design changes; not merely a stimulus-source citation.
